subject: general
question: Which of the following is the birthplace of the founder of Christianity?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bethlehem.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bethlehem**

 
 
• **​**Bethlehem is a city in** Palestine's West Bank**. It is about** 6.2 miles **(or 10 km) south of **Jerusalem.**
 
• It is home to approximately** 25,000 people** and serves as the Bethlehem Governorate's capital.
 
• The city's economy is largely dependent on **tourism**; Around Christmas, when Christians make a pilgrimage to the **Church of the Nativity**, which is regarded as the site of Jesus' Nativity, international tourism peaks.
 
• **Rachel's Tomb,** the burial ground of the **biblical matriarch Rachel**, can be found at the city's northern entrance. The** Israeli West Bank** barrier restricts movement throughout the city.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Galilee**

 
 
• Between **northern Israel and southern Lebanon** is the region known as Galilee. The mountainous region of Upper and Lower Galilee is traditionally referred to as Galilee.
 
• The term "Galilee" refers to the entire region to the south of the** Litani River's east-west section** and north of the **Mount Carmel-Mount Gilboa ridge.**
 
• It stretches from Acre in the west to the **Jordan Rift Valley** in the east, joining the shores of the Mediterranean Sea and the Israeli coastal plain. and from the** Litani to Dan** at the base of Mount Hermon in the northeast, Mount Carmel, and Mount Gilboa in the south, as well as a portion bordering the Golan Heights in the north.
 
 
 
• **Haifa**
 
 
• ​With a population of **285,316 in 2019**, Haifa is Israel's** third-largest city**, behind** Tel Aviv and Jerusalem**. The Haifa metropolitan area, which is Israel's third-most populous, includes the city of Haifa.
 
• It is the location of the **Bahá World Centre**, a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**, and a place where Bahá people go on pilgrimages.
 
 
 
• **Nazareth**
 
 
• **​**The largest city in** Israel's Northern District **is Nazareth. Nazareth is referred to as **"Israel's Arab capital."**
 
• It had **77,445 people** living there in** 2019.** The majority of residents are Israeli Arab citizens, with** 30.9% Christian and 69% Muslim.**
